title: Fog in Ring Topology
description: This scenario explores fog dynamics within a ring communication topology. The disturbance creates coordination challenges that test the agents' ability to adapt, communicate effectively, and maintain freight flow under adverse conditions. The ring topology forces agents to rely on neighbors for information propagation, creating high vulnerability to message delays and stale data during fog events.
edge_cases_to_watch: Agents may observe stale route status
Messages about bridge closures arrive 1 turn late
Agents must decide whether to trust stale observations
Information bottleneck: Agent 'c' becomes a critical relay for 'a' and 'b' due to ring structure
Cascading delays: A delay in high-priority job 'j-004' causes route congestion for 'j-001'
The 'Split-Brain' effect: Agent 'a' and 'c' may have conflicting views of route availability due to the fog-induced message delay
coordination_challenges: Multi-hop information latency: Critical route updates must traverse multiple agents in the ring
Trust arbitration: Discerning between a 'true' route closure and a 'stale' observation during fog
Resource contention: Agents competing for limited capacity on the 'east-north' route (capacity: 1)
Topology-aware rerouting: Calculating paths that account for both physical route capacity and communication constraints
suggested_agent_strategies: Redundancy-based verification: Agents send queries in both directions around the ring to verify route status
Predictive buffering: Agents assume a 1-turn delay in route updates to prevent entering blocked routes
Priority-driven yielding: Lower-priority agents ('normal') yield route capacity to 'high' priority agents proactively
Information aging: Agents discount the reliability of received messages based on the number of hops and time elapsed
